newsitem.title: USA: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - August 1.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - August 1.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING AND MARKETING

CHICAGO - Global advertising company True North Communications Inc says it agreed to buy its smaller rival, Bozell, Jacobs, Kenyon and Eckhardt Inc., in a transaction valued at about $440 million. The deal will create the sixth-largest advertising agency in the world, with more than $11.5 billion in billings and more than 11,000 employees in 297 offices around the world, True North says.

LONDON - Yahoo! Europe, an Internet search and navigation company, will increase its advertising rates in September because of strong demand in categories of business, economics, news and computers, says marketing director Iain Osborne.

DUESSELDORF - Fashion clothing company S. Oliver will invest 12 million marks ($6.5 million) in advertising its brand name on the uniforms of the Borussia Dortmund (BVB 09) soccer team, says Die Welt newspaper.

LONDON - Britain's Glaxo Wellcome Plc says it plans to start advertising its new anti-smoking tablet Zyban directly to consumers in the U.S. later this year. "This is a drug that lends itself to direct-to-consumer advertising," chairman and chief executive Sir Richard Sykes says.

MUNICH - Marketing of products on the Internet is carving a larger niche in the German market and is the most important new trend in direct marketing, says Monika Beumers, director of interactive media at the German Direct Marketing Association (DDV).
WALLDORF - Ad agency Silbermann wins the "customer care" account from Daimler-Benz. The company plans to use the account to train 3,300 car dealers in better customer service.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

MADRID - Canal Satelite Digital, the Canal Plus-backed digital television platform in Spain, says it is filing a complaint with the European Union Competition Commission against Telefonica de Espana, which leads the rival Via Digital platform, over Telefonica's purchase of a 25 percent stake in Antena 3 television station and a controlling stake in its GMA subsiduary.

NEW YORK - Time Warner Inc's Turner Broadcasting System unit says it will convert the structure of its TBS television "superstation" on December 31, to a so-called free market, copyright-paid "superstation", allowing Turner to have a dual revenue stream from both advertising and from subscriber fees paid by cable system operators.

HONG KONG - CCT Telecom Holdings Ltd says it aims to make huge strides into China's paging market following a deal with a Ministry of Electronics Industry-linked company to form joint ventures in China. CCT China Ltd, which will be 67 percent-owned by CCT Telecom and 33 percent-owned by Tesonic International Ltd, is set to create three Sino-foreign joint ventures.
PARIS - Oracle chairman Larry Ellison will join Apple Computer Inc's board and present a new management team next week led by Steve Jobs, Apple's co-founder, says financial newspaper La Tribune.

SYDNEY - News Ltd, the Australian arm of Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd, says it has appointed Aileen Berry as director of corporate affairs. Berry replaces Geraldine Paton, who resigned from the company's board and stepped down as corporate affairs director last month.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

NEW YORK - Music giant PolyGram NV is planning a reorganization within management ranks at its U.S. music operations, The Wall Street Journal says. The company is expected to elevate Danny Goldberg, president and chief executive of its Mercury Records unit, to a broader corporate role while final plans are being worked out, says the paper.

BRUSSELS - Sales of wide-screen televisions in the European Union are doubling every year and should reach 1.3 million in 1997, the European Commission says. The Commission attributes part of the growth to a European Union action plan that has allocated 228 million ecus ($243.6 million) since 1993 to promote broadcasts in the cinema-style 16:9 format.

LONDON - John McGrath, chief executive of Grand Metropolitan Plc, calls for calm negotiation in the tussle with rebel shareholder Bernard Arnault, chairman of French luxury goods company LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton. McGrath, who will fill the role of chief executive of GMG Brands, the name given to the proposed 24 billion pound ($39.3 billion) merger between Guinness Plc and GrandMet, stresses the need to find common ground.
LONDON - Giant Anglo-Dutch consumer group Unilever Plc/NV expects profits growth in the remainder of the year to be less buoyant, chairman Niall Fitzgerald says in a statement.
LONDON - Vendome Luxury Goods Plc says it has agreed to acquire Lancel, the French leather goods group for an estimated 342 million Swiss francs ($225.6 million).

WASHINGTON - Caffeine is a mildly addictive drug linked to miscarriages and other health problems and should be more closely regulated by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, a group of consumer and health experts says. Consumers have a right to know how much caffeine is added by manufacturers to soft drinks, ice creams, yogurt and other foods, according to the Center for Science in the Public Interest.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

PARIS - Tourists are flocking to France in greater numbers than ever before with Mickey Mouse's European residence the main attraction by far. France's national tourism federation says business is booming, bolstered by currency trends that have cut the cost of a French holiday for many travellers.

LONDON - Yahoo! Europe, a provider of Internet search engines, says that a new survey shows its average user is an affluent, professional man, aged 25 to 44. Yahoo! Europe said the survey of 12,394 Yahoo! users in Britain, France and Germany showed users have an average household income of $56,300.
